messages:
pager-bot: 🚨 Pager alert — elevated 5xx rate observed for model-runner-prod (us-west2, svc: inference-gateway). Error class: SIGSEGV / OOM suspects. 5m spike at 08:22 UTC. Notified on-call.
sara_oncall: On it. I'm looking at the gateway dashboards now — p50 latency up 200ms, p95 up 1.2s, 502/504 surge ~8% of requests. Triage channel created.
kevin_runtime: grabbing recent node logs from the runtime pool. seeing repeated segfault backtraces in model-runner container: `libml_infer.so(+0x1a3f2) ...` core files landing on /var/crash/model-runner.
matt_ops: I can isolate nodes and start draining. Suggest immediate slow-down: reroute traffic for heavy customers to dedicated pool while we triage.
kevin_runtime: confirm stack traces show `kv_cache::deserialize` inside attention kernel on hot paths. Could be corrupted KV cache growth causing page faults.
emily_support: flagged customers who hit >5% error rate: acme-hr, fintools. Notifying account teams and setting mitigation banner.
devon_eng: quick mitigation: enable model fallback routing to quantized-8 model variant for the gateway in us-west2, and reduce batch window to 8ms to limit memory pressure. Can we do that safely?
kevin_runtime: fallback config ready. Deploying policy change: `route_policy set --region us-west2 --model * --fallback model-edu-q8 --max_batch_ms 8` (dry-run then apply).
sara_oncall: Apply now. Start draining 3 nodes with repeated crash signatures. Matt, schedule node-restarts with `systemctl restart model-runner` after drain.
matt_ops: draining node-14, node-15. Restarting model-runner on node-14 — will monitor for repeat crash.
kevin_runtime: attaching a short log snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T08:20:45Z] model-runner[pid:4321]: INFO KVCache::size=1.2GB
[2026-03-17T08:20:46Z] model-runner[pid:4321]: WARNING attention_kernel: tuning path switch
[2026-03-17T08:20:47Z] model-runner[pid:4321]: ERROR segfault at 0x7ff... in kv_cache.cpp:line 412
[2026-03-17T08:20:47Z] kernel: RIP: 0x7f... libml_infer.so+0x1a3f2
```
kevin_runtime: core size ~1.1GB, looks like late-stage allocation failure followed by invalid read. Could be memory corruption under peak prefix lengths.
devon_eng: adding temporary guard: `RLIMIT_AS` limit reduced for process so it OOMs earlier and avoids corrupting heap; also enable `kvcache.prefetch=false` to disable async prefetch. Rolling those flags to canary.
kevin_runtime: canary deploy applied to 2 nodes — no segfaults in 6m. Error rate for routed traffic dropped to 1.2%. Gateway 5xx now at 1.8% overall.
emily_support: pushing status to affected customers: short note that we detected runtime crashes, have a progressive mitigation (fallback model + config flags) and are routing traffic to dedicated capacity for high-importance tenants.
sara_oncall: preparing handoff notes for follow-up window. We'll keep incident live until root cause confirmed. Next on-call: @alice_research take postmortem lead for model-level investigation; @matt_ops continue node restarts + triage.
alice_research: acknowledged. I'll pull model artifacts, run inference locally with long prefix tests and sanitizers. Also will run `valgrind --leak-check=full` on a dev build to try to reproduce heap corruption.
matt_ops: documenting node list and actions in the incident doc. Nodes drained: node-14, node-15; canary nodes: node-21, node-22. Rollback plan: revert routing policy to original if error rate <1% for 30m.
sara_oncall: customer impact summary for handoff: brief spike of 5xx affecting ~0.5% of total traffic peak, 2 enterprise customers saw degraded service. No data loss reported. SLA breach risk: low but need postmortem.
kevin_runtime: next steps: upload compressed core dumps to secure bucket `s3://redwood-incidents/3222223333/cores/`, run `gdb -c core --batch -ex \"thread apply all bt\"` and share sanitized stack. Also investigate kvcache growth metrics.
sara_oncall: handing off to on-call + followups. Handoff ETA: 10:00 UTC. Last message before handoff: ensure pager alerts suppressed for the routed fallback so we don't get duplicate noise. :thumbsup:
